title: Former Vatican envoy to the Philippines passes away
summary: Former apostolic nuncio to the Philippines Archbishop Antonio Franco has died on November 15, 2026, CBCP News reported.

blocks.text: Former apostolic nuncio to the Philippines Archbishop Antonio Franco has died on November 15, 2026, CBCP News reported.
Franco was the diplomatic representative of the Vatican to the Philippines from 1999 to 2006. He was 89.
The announcement was made by Bishop Giuseppe Mazzafaro of Cerreto Sannita-Telese-Sant’Agata de’ Goti, who also expressed his condolences to the family and those who shared his priestly ministry.
CBCP News reported that Franco died at Rummo Hospital in Benevento, where he had been admitted a few days earlier.
The Italian diplomat spent seven years in the Philippines, from 1999 to 2006, before he was assigned to the Middle East.

"His tenure coincided with the 2001 EDSA II People Power uprising and the reorganization of the Archdiocese of Manila, which resulted in the creation of new dioceses in the capital region," the report stated.

Franco was born in Puglianello, Italy, on March 24, 1937 and was ordained a priest for the Diocese of Cerreto Sannita-Telese-Sant’Agata de’ Goti on July 10, 1960 and entered the Vatican diplomatic service in 1972 and served in Bolivia, Iran and France, and at the Holy See’s permanent mission to the United Nations in New York.

Franco was the first Vatican representative to the country following its independence from the Soviet Union. He was also apostolic nuncio to Israel and Cyprus and apostolic delegate to Jerusalem and Palestine.
Franco retired from diplomatic service in August 2012.

CBCP News also reported that Franco’s remains arrived Nov. 16 at the Parish of St. James the Apostle in Puglianello, where a wake held. A funeral Mass is scheduled for Tuesday at the Church of St. Alphonsus Maria de’ Liguori in Telese Terme. — BAP, GMA News
